title: A small shared step for MPS I families: proposal to MPS Society (UK)

sentences.text: At Canadian MPS Society, we share your commitment to families affected by IDUA-related MPS I: Hurler, Hurler-Scheie and Scheie.
MPS I and MPS II (Hunter syndrome) both involve missing enzyme activity and a build-up of substances inside cells.
The atlas also infers similar symptoms, but that connection has confidence 0.49, below 0.5; sharing research approaches is a possibility to explore, not a proven fit.

sections.heading: What already exists that we could share

sentences.text: The Canadian MPS Registry, Mucopolysaccharidosis I (MPS I) Registry and Registry of Patients Diagnosed With Lysosomal Storage Diseases are listed as resources for MPS I.
The input marks these resources as reusable as-is because they cover this disease; we propose sharing information about them first, rather than assuming access to patient data.

sections.heading: What must be checked before we join forces

sentences.text: Please help confirm whether low tissue alpha-L-iduronidase activity and hand pain also occur in MPS II.
We should also check underdevelopment of the rounded top of the thigh bone, and review all three features before extending comparisons to Gaucher disease or acid sphingomyelinase deficiency.
Please treat missing symptom records as questions, not proof that a feature is absent.
We should verify study eligibility and permission to reuse resources before making any commitments.
Send one focused inquiry to MPS Society (UK), asking whether Mucopolysaccharidosis Type II Natural History could include people with MPS I, with the symptom checks above attached.
No open questions are recorded yet.
We would welcome a small collaboration for MPS I families.
Your organization and ours both support this community.
Could you help us explore whether Mucopolysaccharidosis Type II Natural History could include MPS I?
We suggest starting with the eligibility and symptom checks, without assuming the study can expand.
Thank you for considering this first conversation.
[Your name], on behalf of Canadian MPS Society
